boil_off.basis: Conduction through the insulation at the upper ambient design air temperature (IGC Code 7.2), over the latent heat of methane (NIST saturation table); domes, saddles and pipes are not in the heat leak. The conductivity is an Estimate.

boil_off_detail.u_value_basis: Heat leak of one tank over its outer area (a cylinder and two heads taken as a sphere, on the outer radius) and the temperature difference; domes, saddles and pipes are not in it.

holding_time.basis: Homogeneous closed-tank model of methane (one saturation state, no thermal stratification: the real pressure can rise faster), stepped every 10 minutes (second order) from the loading limit at the start pressure (IGC Code 15.1.3.1). The heat leak is recomputed each step at the IGC Code 7.2 air ambient (45 C) over the whole tank surface. The gas use credited on a passage leg is the least gas use of the powering model across its service conditions, at its service speed. The leg records its passage speed (the typed one, else the design service speed, as the profile input resolves it), but the credit is not yet worked out at that speed and at the lightest draught of the leg: that link to the powering model belongs to issues #871 and #875. The series is kept every 6 h plus the end of each leg and the last point. Domes, saddles and pipes are not in the heat leak. Methane stands in for the LNG composition.

boil_off.basis: Conduction through the insulation at the upper ambient design air temperature (IGC Code 7.2), over the latent heat of methane (NIST saturation table); domes, saddles and pipes are not in the heat leak. The conductivity is an Estimate.

boil_off_detail.u_value_basis: Heat leak of one tank over its outer area (a cylinder and two heads taken as a sphere, on the outer radius) and the temperature difference; domes, saddles and pipes are not in it.

holding_time.basis: Homogeneous closed-tank model of methane (one saturation state, no thermal stratification: the real pressure can rise faster), stepped every 10 minutes (second order) from the loading limit at the start pressure (IGC Code 15.1.3.1). The heat leak is recomputed each step at the IGC Code 7.2 air ambient (45 C) over the whole tank surface. The gas use credited on a passage leg is the least gas use of the powering model across its service conditions, at its service speed. The leg records its passage speed (the typed one, else the design service speed, as the profile input resolves it), but the credit is not yet worked out at that speed and at the lightest draught of the leg: that link to the powering model belongs to issues #871 and #875. The series is kept every 6 h plus the end of each leg and the last point. Domes, saddles and pipes are not in the heat leak. Methane stands in for the LNG composition.
